issues.legal_issue: A tenant seeking leave to contest a summary eviction petition based on the landlord’s bona fide requirement must receive leave when the tenant’s affidavit raises non-frivolous facts that could defeat the landlord’s entitlement and require adjudication at trial.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction on the ground of bona fide requirement and relied on a registered sale deed to establish ownership.

The tenants disputed the landlord’s title, alleging that the property had vested in a public custodian and could not validly have been sold to the landlord; they also challenged the genuineness of the sale deed and the sellers’ title.
The tenants produced a communication from the custodian stating that the property vested in it and that rent was to be collected on its behalf.
The Rent Controller relied on an earlier order under a different property statute declaring the property not to be evacuee property and denied leave to defend; the High Court affirmed.

The Supreme Court held that the questions of vesting, the consequences of vesting, and the sale deed’s authenticity required determination at trial, and that the tenants’ pleas were not frivolous or baseless.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed, the orders denying leave were set aside, and the tenants were granted leave to defend the eviction petition so the rival claims could be decided after the parties had an opportunity to prove their cases.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 25B(5) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, a tenant must be given leave to contest an eviction application under Section 14(1)(e) if the affidavit discloses facts that would disentitle the landlord from obtaining possession. The leave-stage inquiry is summary and asks whether the tenant has disclosed reasonable grounds; it concerns disclosure of facts, not proof of them. Rent-control legislation should not be construed hyper-technically in a way that frustrates its protective purpose. The Court relied on Mangat Ram v. Kedar Nath, 1980 (4) SCC 276.

rule.if: summary_eviction_leave_request and tenant_discloses_material_defense and defense_not_frivolous and defense_requires_trial

predicates.summary_eviction_leave_request: A tenant asks for leave to contest a landlord’s summary eviction petition based on a claimed need for the premises.
predicates.tenant_discloses_material_defense: The tenant’s affidavit sets out facts which, if established, could defeat the landlord’s entitlement to possession.
predicates.defense_not_frivolous: The tenant’s stated grounds have a prima facie basis and are not baseless or unreal.
predicates.defense_requires_trial: The disputed matters require evidence and adjudication rather than resolution in the summary leave inquiry.

issues.definition: When a tenant seeks leave in a summary eviction proceeding and presents a prima facie, material defense requiring trial, the tenant is allowed to defend the eviction claim.
